about.title: Sources and method
about.method: This project separates documented facts, interpretation and tradition, and labels each entry with its certainty level. No dates, people or coordinates are invented: anything unverified is flagged.
about.coords: Locations: positions are approximate and being verified on the ground. Each entry states its accuracy.
about.tourism: Visitor information: hours and fares come from official sites, with the date they were checked. They may change.

scene.artistic: Artistic interpretation · not an archaeological reconstruction
scene.illustration: Illustration · free recreation, not to scale
scene.pre.aria: Animation: the coast before the city, with mangroves, early pottery, a village with canoes and the arrival of ships in 1533.
scene.pre.1b: A coast of mangroves, lagoons and bays, with La Popa hill in the distance.
scene.pre.2b: Some of the oldest pottery in the Americas has been found in this region.
scene.pre.3b: Indigenous communities lived off the sea and the lagoons. The chronicles call this place Calamarí.
scene.pre.4b: Pedro de Heredia’s ships arrive. A new story begins.
scene.gal.aria: Animation: the San José galleon sails, blows up in battle in 1708, sinks, and is now studied on the seabed.
scene.gal.1b: The Spanish fleet sails for Cartagena. Off Barú, a British squadron lies in wait.
scene.gal.2b: In the middle of the battle, the San José blows up.
scene.gal.3b: It sinks with some 600 people on board. Only 11 survive.
scene.gal.4b: The Navy finds it on the seabed. Today scientists study it; its location is classified.
